## Natural history notes

A large nonnative treefrog characterized by its warty skin, large toe pads, bulging eyes, and variable gray, tan, brown, or green coloration. In Florida, it is commonly found in urban and suburban areas, gardens, yards, wetlands, tree cavities, buildings, and other moist sheltered habitats. It is mostly active at night and feeds on insects, small frogs, lizards, and other small animals, often outcompeting or preying on native treefrogs.
